title: Micro-Macro Coupled Koopman Modeling on Graph for Traffic Flow Prediction
claim: A traffic scene becomes a vehicle-centric graph, and two coupled encoder-evolver-decoder branches jointly predict individual trajectories and aggregate flow density.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right; road scene feeds two parallel branches with cross-links
description: A wide single-panel pipeline diagram. At far left is a photo-like top-down road scene with a gray multilane road. Yellow and teal cars are linked by black edges inside a dashed rounded box, and one ego vehicle is circled. An arrow points up from the ego vehicle to a formula box with the vehicle state x_t^e = [p, v, l, s]. A second arrow points down, labeled r_max and k-NN, to a graph formula box G_t = (V_t, E_t, W_t). From these boxes, two rows of dark-teal rounded boxes run left to right. The top row is VK Encoder, Intent Discriminator, IntentAware VKEvolver, VK Decode, then Predicted Trajectory. The bottom row is GK Encoder, GKEvolver, GK Decode, then Predicted Density. A central Fusing box links the two rows with vertical arrows. White text on dark boxes draws the eye along the arrows.
caption: We propose a Micro-Macro Coupled Koopman Modeling (MMCKM) framework that lifts microscopic vehicle trajectories and macroscopic flow evolution into linear observation spaces, enabling unified prediction. The traffic environment is formulated as a directed graph. At the macroscopic level, vehicle-centric graph discretization captures how microscopic perturbations affect wave propagation. At the microscopic level, scenario-adaptive Koopman operators and Koopman control incorporate macroscopic flow conditions into vehicle dynamics.
abstract: Traffic systems are inherently multi-scale: microscopic vehicle interactions and macroscopic flow co-evolve nonlinearly. Microscopic models capture local interactions but miss flow evolution; macroscopic models enforce aggregated consistency yet overlook stochastic vehicle-level dynamics. We propose Micro–Macro Coupled Koopman Modeling (MMCKM), which lifts the coupled dynamics to a high-dimensional linear observation space for a unified linear-operator representation. Unlike grid-based discretizations, MMCKM adopts a vehicle-centric dynamic graph that preserves microscopic perturbations while respecting macroscopic conservation laws by discretizing PDEs onto this graph. At the micro scale, scenario-adaptive Koopman evolvers selected by an Intent Discriminator are designed to model vehicle dynamics. A Koopman control module explicitly formulate how flow state influences individual vehicles, yielding bidirectional couplings. To our knowledge, this is the first work to jointly model vehicle trajectories and traffic flow density using a unified Koopman framework without requiring historical trajectories. The proposed MMCKM is validated for trajectory prediction on NGSIM and HighD. While MMCKM uses only real-time measurement, it achieves comparable or even higher accuracy than history-dependent baselines. We further analyze the effect of the operator interval and provide ablations to show the improvement by intent inference, macro-to-micro control, and diffusion. Code and implementation details are included to facilitate reproducibility.
